Milo: 14 Facts the Tanking Women in Tech Movement Doesnt Want You to Know

Women’s Brains Aren’t As Well Suited To Programming As Men’s

Sadly, using a sample size of one, it's true. I'm a woman and I've done a fair bit of coding in my day, but I can attest that I struggled with things my male colleagues seemed to sail through. I did better in languages that were closer to spoken language (Perl, scripting languages) and worse as it got closer to machine code.

I will say, I occasionally came up with brilliantly weird solutions to problems that would not have occurred to my coworkers, but I suspect that's more because I'm eccentric than because I'm female. Also, I worked in multimedia, so when I fucked something up in an idiosyncratic way, nobody died.

Nobody is the best at anything, ever. People often judge performance and ability on a hard-to-interpret and often plainly subjective scale, but even when that's not the case the person in question could reasonably be expected to preform better or worse at a similar but tangentially different task, or at the same task at a different time.

Point is, everything should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis, or not at all. Are men generally more suited to programming than women? It seems that way a lot of the time, but that's irrelevant since proficient programmers need the rest of the species to become useful in the role of proficient programmer.

This got more meta than I intended, but fuck it I took the time to write it.
